newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Train crash in Pakistan kills at least 35.
newsitem.headline: Train crash in Pakistan kills at least 35.

text.p: At least 35 people were killed and 60 injured in a train crash near Khanewal town in Pakistan's central province of Punjab, on Monday, police said.

They said a Karachi-bound passenger train had failed to stop at a junction and controllers had diverted it onto a dead-end track to prevent a head-on collision with a Lahore-Karachi express train coming the other way on the single main track.
The diverted train hit the buffers at the end of the spur line near the village of Mirshah, about five km (three miles) from Khanewal, derailing the engine and five coaches.
The accident happened at about 4.30 a.m. (2330 GMT Sunday).
Rescue workers were using blow-torches to cut the injured free from the wreckage. They said at least 60 people had been taken to hospital and the death toll could rise further.
On January 21, an express train hit a school van at a level crossing at Gujarhan, 60 km (37 miles) south of Islamabad, killing nine people, including six children and two teachers.
